title: TOOLS-GITIGNORE-001: make repository tooling namespaces normally trackable
intent: Repair the blanket /tools/ ignore footgun where new source files under established repository-owned tooling namespaces were silently ignored (requiring git add -f). Change repository tracking policy only: ignore loose content directly under tools/ by default, but explicitly un-ignore the established namespaces (grounding_agent, agent_program, codegen) and the tools/ custody README, while generated Python artifacts stay ignored via the existing global __pycache__/ and *.pyc rules. Adds a deterministic git check-ignore regression pinning both sides of the boundary and a tools/README.md documenting it. No production, Agent Program, or Grounding Agent behavior changes.

diff_articulation.what_changed: Replaces the blanket `/tools/` ignore with `/tools/*` plus negations `!/tools/README.md`, `!/tools/grounding_agent/`, `!/tools/agent_program/`, `!/tools/codegen/` (root-anchored, preserving the Dec-2025 nested-app-code anchoring). Adds tests/governance/test_tools_gitignore_boundary.py (git check-ignore witnesses for both sides) and tools/README.md documenting the custody boundary. No other ignore rules changed; global __pycache__//*.pyc rules continue to suppress generated Python artifacts.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: No prior rule or test made the tracked tooling namespaces normally stageable — new files under them were silently ignored, and the only prior mitigation was ad-hoc git add -f. This turns the intended policy into an executable, enforced contract; nothing existing provides it.

commands_run: python -m pytest tests/governance/test_tools_gitignore_boundary.py -> 5 fail pre-repair (trackable side), 14 pass post-repair
python -m pytest tests/agent_program/ -> 19 passed, 1 skipped (Agent Program unchanged)
git status --short -> only .gitignore (M) + tools/README.md + the test (no unexpected newly-visible files swept in)
